::: {.callout-important}
## Recommendation in one box

**Calibrate every model slot (a11–a15) by MAXIMISING the equally weighted average of the two
metrics that will be reported:**

$$
\mathcal{O} \;=\; 0.5\,\mathrm{KGE}\!\left(Q_{\text{sim}},Q_{\text{obs}}\right)
            \;+\; 0.5\,\mathrm{NSE}\!\left(Q_{\text{sim}},Q_{\text{obs}}\right)
$$

on **untransformed** daily flow (mm/day), KGE as defined by @gupta2009 and NSE by @nash1970
(the project's canonical `src/common/metrics.py`), evaluated on the **calibration metric window
1952-10-01 … 1988-09-30 (13 149 days)**, warm-up 1951-10-01 … 1952-09-30 excluded.
Optimisers that minimise use the cost $1-\mathcal{O}$ (perfect = 0, unbounded above).
Implementation: `src.common.metrics_extra.objective` / `objective_cost`; contract:
`config/metrics.yaml`.

*No transform and therefore no offset $\varepsilon$ anywhere.* Observed $Q\ge0.069$ mm/day on all
14 610 days, so $\sqrt{\cdot}$, $\log$ and Box–Cox **would** be defined without an arbitrary
constant (@sec-why) — the point is that they are not needed: a third $\mathrm{KGE}(\sqrt{Q})$ term
was tested explicitly and changed every out-of-sample number by less than 0.001.

*Why not plain KGE, the ranking metric?* Because @sec-transfer calibrates two surrogate
rainfall–runoff models under **24 candidate objectives** on **four independent splits inside the
calibration period** (three of them 20–46 % wetter than their training years, mimicking the
evaluation window, which is 29 % wetter than calibration). Result, as mean shortfall behind the
best objective of each of the 8 experiments ("regret"):

| objective used for calibration | regret in KGE | regret in NSE | worst case KGE | worst case NSE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **0.5·KGE + 0.5·NSE (recommended)** | 0.026 | 0.017 | **0.056** | **0.047** |
| KGE alone | **0.020** | 0.047 | 0.039 | 0.162 |
| NSE alone | 0.052 | **0.003** | 0.107 | 0.010 |
| KGE(√Q) | 0.024 | 0.019 | 0.067 | 0.063 |

KGE alone and NSE alone each win *their own* metric and lose badly on the other; the 50/50 average
is the only candidate whose **worst case stays below 0.06 on both metrics simultaneously**. KGE and
NSE are not redundant on this record — their Spearman rank correlation over behavioural simulations
is ≈0.7 (@fig-objcorr) — so the average is a genuine compromise rather than a re-weighting.

Trainable models (a09, LSTM) minimise the identical quantity as a **full-batch** loss
(population standard deviations); a per-mini-batch KGE is a different objective.

**Reported metrics are fixed and are NOT chosen here:** a16 reports **KGE and NSE on untransformed
$Q$** only, ranked by KGE, per `config/project.yaml`.
:::

# Scope and constraints {#sec-scope}

The metrics in the *final* report are fixed by the user and by `config/project.yaml`
(`evaluation_protocol.required_metrics: [KGE, NSE]`, `primary_selection_metric: KGE`,
`final_report_metrics_only: true`). Agent 4 therefore does **not** choose the reporting metrics.
What Agent 4 chooses is the **calibration objective**: the scalar that a10's optimisers and
a11–a15's calibration runs drive to its optimum. Objective $\ne$ reporting metric is a deliberate
and well-documented distinction [@clark2021; @mizukami2019]: the objective is an *estimator design
choice* whose only job is to put parameters where the reported metrics will be good **on data the
calibration never saw**.

Three hard boundary conditions frame the choice:

| # | Constraint | Consequence for the objective |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Report = KGE and NSE on raw $Q$; KGE decides the ranking | The objective must be dominated by an untransformed KGE term; an objective built purely on transformed flows optimises the wrong thing |
| 2 | Evaluation window (1949-01-01…1951-09-30) is the **wettest** stretch of the record: mean $Q$ 1.749 vs 1.353 mm/d (ratio 1.29), runoff ratio 0.41 vs 0.35, 1.7 % of days above the calibration $Q_{99}$, but max 45.9 mm/d **below** the calibration max 64.0 mm/d | No magnitude extrapolation is needed, but the objective must not buy calibration score by over-fitting the few largest floods, and must control the volume ratio $\beta$, which is what shifts under a wet transfer |
| 3 | Only 92 warm-up days precede the evaluation metric window | Objectives that depend on long-memory low-flow behaviour (log, $1/Q$) are the most exposed to initial-state error early in 1949 |

: Boundary conditions imposed on the objective choice. {#tbl-constraints}

# Catalogue of metrics {#sec-catalogue}

All formulas use $s_i$ = simulated and $o_i$ = observed daily flow (mm/day), $i=1\dots n$ over the
metric window, $\mu$ = mean, $\sigma$ = standard deviation (population), $r$ = Pearson correlation.
Every metric listed here is implemented in `src/common/metrics_extra.py` and registered in
`mx.METRICS`, with `mx.ORIENTATION` (+1 larger-is-better, −1 smaller-is-better, 0 target-value) and
`mx.OPTIMUM`. `KGE` and `NSE` themselves are imported from the canonical `src/common/metrics.py`.

## Squared-error family

$$
\mathrm{MSE}=\frac1n\sum (s_i-o_i)^2,\qquad \mathrm{RMSE}=\sqrt{\mathrm{MSE}},\qquad
\mathrm{NSE}=1-\frac{\sum (s_i-o_i)^2}{\sum (o_i-\mu_o)^2}
$$

$$
\mathrm{NSE}_{T}=1-\frac{\sum (T(s_i)-T(o_i))^2}{\sum (T(o_i)-\mu_{T(o)})^2},\quad
T\in\{\sqrt{\cdot},\ \log,\ 1/\cdot,\ \text{Box–Cox}_\lambda\},\qquad
\mathrm{NNSE}=\frac{1}{2-\mathrm{NSE}}
$$

@gupta2009 decomposition, used throughout this report:
$$
\mathrm{NSE}=2\alpha r-\alpha^2-\beta_n^2,\qquad
\alpha=\frac{\sigma_s}{\sigma_o},\quad \beta_n=\frac{\mu_s-\mu_o}{\sigma_o}.
$$

```{python}
#| label: tbl-cat-sse
#| tbl-cap: "Squared-error family. 'Sens.' = which part of the hydrograph dominates the score."

 ("sqrt-NSE", r"$\mathrm{NSE}$ on $\sqrt{Q}$", "(−∞,1]", "1", "–", "balanced (mid/high)", "variance-stabilising for Poisson-like skew; keeps peaks relevant", "no closed-form diagnostic split", "@oudin2006"),
```

## KGE family

$$
\mathrm{KGE}=1-\sqrt{(r-1)^2+(\alpha-1)^2+(\beta-1)^2},\qquad
\alpha=\frac{\sigma_s}{\sigma_o},\quad \beta=\frac{\mu_s}{\mu_o}
$$

```{python}
#| label: tbl-cat-kge
#| tbl-cap: "KGE family. All are +1-oriented with optimum 1 and are dimensionless."
rows = [
 ("KGE (2009)", r"$1-\sqrt{(r-1)^2+(\alpha-1)^2+(\beta-1)^2}$", "(−∞,1]", "balanced", "explicit, orthogonal control of timing, variability and volume; project ranking metric", "mean-flow benchmark is −0.41, not 0 [@knoben2019]", "@gupta2009"),
 ("KGE′ (2012)", r"$\gamma=\frac{\sigma_s/\mu_s}{\sigma_o/\mu_o}$ replaces $\alpha$", "(−∞,1]", "balanced", "removes the correlation between the $\\alpha$ and $\\beta$ terms", "$\\gamma$ is blind to a pure scaling error, so bias is penalised only once", "@kling2012"),
 ("KGE″ (2021)", r"$\beta_n=\frac{\mu_s-\mu_o}{\sigma_o}$ replaces $\beta$", "(−∞,1]", "balanced", "stable when $\\mu_o\\to0$ (ephemeral rivers)", "at CV = 2.11 the bias term almost disappears — becomes NSE-like (@sec-why)", "@tang2021"),
 ("non-parametric KGE", r"Spearman $r_S$, FDC-based $\alpha_{NP}=1-\tfrac12\sum|\tfrac{s_{(k)}}{n\mu_s}-\tfrac{o_{(k)}}{n\mu_o}|$", "(−∞,1]", "balanced, robust", "insensitive to the extreme tail; compares full FDC shape", "loses information on the magnitude of individual events", "@pool2018"),
 ("KGE on $T(Q)$", r"KGE of $\sqrt{Q}$, $\log Q$, $1/Q$", "(−∞,1]", "set by $T$", "shifts emphasis while keeping the 3-way decomposition", "log-KGE is dominated by the smallest flows; $\\beta$ on logs is not a volume ratio [@santos2018]", "@santos2018"),

 ("split KGE", r"$\frac1m\sum_j \mathrm{KGE}_j$ over sub-periods $j$", "(−∞,1]", "balanced in time", "exposes non-stationary performance; robust to one dominant year", "noisy for short windows", "@fowler2018"),
```

## Event / peak, FDC-segment and signature metrics

These are **diagnostics**, never the objective here (they are not differentiable, not smooth, and
several are undefined for poor simulations). They are used in @sec-transfer to explain *why* an

::: {.callout-note}
## Information-theoretic and probabilistic scores
Mutual information $I(s;o)$, CRPS and Wasserstein distances were considered. CRPS requires a
predictive *distribution*; all five model slots are deterministic and the final ranking is
deterministic, so CRPS is only meaningful if an ensemble is submitted — it is therefore not part of
the objective and not part of the report. The 1-Wasserstein distance between FDCs **is** implemented
(`FDC_W1_log`) because it is a pure distribution-shape diagnostic: a model can have $W_1=0$ and
$r=0$, which makes it a clean complement to KGE's $r$ term. Mutual information was rejected as an
objective: on 13 149 daily values it needs binning/KDE choices that are themselves tuning
parameters, and it is invariant to any monotone transform — including a 50 % volume bias.
:::

# Why this particular data set constrains the choice {#sec-why}

```{python}
#| label: fig-leverage
#| fig-cap: "Leverage of the largest flows. Left: share of total volume and of the NSE denominator $\\sum(o-\\mu_o)^2$ carried by the wettest days (calibration metric window). Right: the same share of the squared-error 'gradient mass' under three transforms."
s_sorted = np.sort(O)[::-1]
frac = np.arange(1, len(O) + 1) / len(O)
cum_vol = np.cumsum(s_sorted) / s_sorted.sum()
d2 = (s_sorted - O.mean()) ** 2
cum_ss = np.cumsum(d2) / d2.sum()

lev = {}
for nm, x in (("$Q$", O), ("$\\sqrt{Q}$", np.sqrt(O)), ("$\\log Q$", np.log(O))):
    xs = np.sort(x)[::-1]; dd = (xs - x.mean()) ** 2
    lev[nm] = np.cumsum(dd) / dd.sum()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9.5, 3.4))
ax[0].plot(100 * frac, 100 * cum_vol, label="share of total volume")
ax[0].plot(100 * frac, 100 * cum_ss, label=r"share of $\sum(o-\mu_o)^2$ (NSE denominator)")
ax[0].set_xscale("log"); ax[0].set_xlim(0.05, 100); ax[0].set_xlabel("wettest x % of days")
ax[0].set_ylabel("cumulative share (%)"); ax[0].legend(loc="lower right")
ax[0].axvline(1, color="0.5", lw=0.8, ls=":"); ax[0].axvline(5, color="0.5", lw=0.8, ls=":")
ax[0].set_title("Volume vs squared-error leverage")
for nm, v in lev.items():
    ax[1].plot(100 * frac, 100 * v, label=nm)
ax[1].set_xscale("log"); ax[1].set_xlim(0.05, 100); ax[1].set_xlabel("wettest x % of days")
ax[1].set_ylabel("share of $\\sum(T(o)-\\mu)^2$ (%)"); ax[1].legend(title="transform")
ax[1].axvline(1, color="0.5", lw=0.8, ls=":"); ax[1].axvline(5, color="0.5", lw=0.8, ls=":")
ax[1].set_title("Effect of the transform on leverage")
save(fig, "leverage"); plt.show()

tbl = []
for p in (0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10):
    k = int(p * len(O))
    row = {"wettest % of days": 100 * p, "% of volume": 100 * s_sorted[:k].sum() / s_sorted.sum()}
    for nm, x in (("Q", O), ("sqrt Q", np.sqrt(O)), ("log Q", np.log(O))):
        xs = np.sort(x)[::-1]; dd = (xs - x.mean()) ** 2
        row[f"% of SS ({nm})"] = 100 * dd[:k].sum() / dd.sum()
    tbl.append(row)
LEVERAGE = pd.DataFrame(tbl)
md(LEVERAGE.round(1), index=False)
```

**Fact 1 — one per cent of the days own the squared-error criterion.** In the calibration metric
window the wettest 1 % of days (131 of 13 149) carry 15.7 % of the volume but **58.3 %** of
$\sum(o-\mu_o)^2$; the wettest 5 % carry 83.6 %. Any SSE-based objective (MSE, RMSE, NSE, Gaussian
likelihood — all with the same argmax) is therefore, in effect, fitted to ~130 flood days.
The $\sqrt{\cdot}$ transform reduces the 1 % share to 26.8 % and $\log$ to 8.7 %: these numbers,
not a preference, are what "balancing high and low flows" means here.

**Fact 2 — NSE is nearly blind to volume bias at this CV, KGE is not.** For a simulation with the
right shape but a volume ratio $\beta=c$ ($r=1$, $\alpha=c$),

$$
\mathrm{KGE}=1-\sqrt2\,|c-1| \quad\text{(both } \alpha \text{ and } \beta \text{ terms)},\qquad
\mathrm{NSE}=1-\Big(\tfrac{c-1}{\mathrm{CV}_o}\Big)^2\ \text{if only the mean is wrong},
$$

and $\mathrm{CV}_o=2.107$ here.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bias-sens
#| tbl-cap: "Penalty of a pure volume error at the Leaf River calibration CV = 2.107. 'KGE (β only)' isolates the volume term; 'NSE (mean only)' is the corresponding NSE loss. The last column is how many times harder KGE punishes the same water-balance error."
rows = []
for c in (0.85, 0.90, 0.95, 1.05, 1.10, 1.20, 1.30):
    dk = abs(c - 1.0)                      # KGE loss from the beta term alone
    dn = ((c - 1.0) / CV_O) ** 2           # NSE loss from the mean alone
    dk_full = np.sqrt(2) * abs(c - 1.0)    # KGE loss when alpha scales too
    rows.append({"β = Q_sim/Q_obs": c, "ΔKGE (β term only)": dk,
                 "ΔKGE (α and β, sim = c·obs)": dk_full,
                 "ΔNSE (mean only)": dn, "ratio ΔKGE/ΔNSE": dk / dn})
BIAS = pd.DataFrame(rows)
md(BIAS.round({"β = Q_sim/Q_obs": 2, "ΔKGE (β term only)": 4, "ΔKGE (α and β, sim = c·obs)": 4,
               "ΔNSE (mean only)": 5, "ratio ΔKGE/ΔNSE": 1}), index=False)
```

A model that is 10 % too wet loses **0.100 KGE but only 0.0023 NSE** — a factor 44. This is the
single most important asymmetry for this project: calibrating on NSE lets the optimiser trade
water balance for a slightly better fit to floods almost for free, and that debt is paid in full in
the KGE ranking — *and it is paid on a period 29 % wetter than the one the trade was made on.*
The same algebra explains why KGE″ [@tang2021], whose bias term is $\beta_n=(\mu_s-\mu_o)/\sigma_o$,
behaves almost like NSE here: at CV = 2.107 it divides the bias by 2.1 before squaring it.

**Fact 3 — no offset $\varepsilon$ is needed.** a02 verified $Q>0$ on all 14 610 days
(min 0.069 mm/day, quantised at 1 ft³/s over 1 949 km²). Every $\log$, $\sqrt{}$, $1/Q$ and Box–Cox
statistic in this report is therefore computed with $\varepsilon=0$, which removes the usual
arbitrary-constant problem [@pushpalatha2012; @santos2018]: an $\varepsilon$ is a hidden tuning
parameter that silently sets *which* low flows the objective can see. Only simulated flows are
floored (at $10^{-12}$ mm/day) so that a degenerate model cannot return $-\infty$.

```{python}
#| label: fig-transform
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of observed daily Q in the calibration metric window under the four candidate transforms (no offset needed: min Q = 0.069 mm/day)."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(11, 2.6))
for a, (nm, x) in zip(ax, [("$Q$", O), ("$\\sqrt{Q}$", np.sqrt(O)),
                           ("Box–Cox $\\lambda=0.25$", mx.t_boxcox(O, 0.25)), ("$\\log Q$", np.log(O))]):
    a.hist(x, bins=60, color="steelblue")
    sk = float(((x - x.mean()) ** 3).mean() / x.std() ** 3)
    a.set_title(f"{nm}\nskew = {sk:.2f}"); a.set_yticks([])
save(fig, "transforms"); plt.show()
```

# Benchmarks {#sec-benchmarks}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-benchmarks
#| tbl-cap: "Reference points on the calibration metric window (1952-10-01…1988-09-30). A model is only skilful above these."
bench = {}
bench["mean flow (constant)"] = mx.benchmark_mean_flow(O)
bench["day-of-year climatology (15-d smoothed)"] = mx.benchmark_climatology(O, IDX[MM], smooth=15)
bench["day-of-year climatology (raw)"] = mx.benchmark_climatology(O, IDX[MM], smooth=1)
pers = np.r_[O[0], O[:-1]]
bench["persistence Q(t) = Q(t-1)"] = {"NSE": nse(pers, O), "KGE": kge(pers, O),
                                      **{k: v for k, v in kge_components(pers, O).items() if k != "KGE"}}
lh = mx._lyne_hollick(O)
bench["baseflow only (Lyne–Hollick)"] = {"NSE": nse(lh, O), "KGE": kge(lh, O),
                                         **{k: v for k, v in kge_components(lh, O).items() if k != "KGE"}}
BENCH = pd.DataFrame(bench).T[["KGE", "NSE", "r", "alpha", "beta"]]
md(BENCH.round(3))
```

The mean-flow benchmark is the reference every reader mis-remembers: **NSE = 0 but KGE = $1-\sqrt2$
= −0.414**, not 0 [@knoben2019]. KGE = 0 is already a *non-trivial* model. A day-of-year climatology
— which uses no forcing at all — reaches KGE ≈ 0.08 / NSE ≈ 0.13 here, and one-day persistence
reaches KGE 0.89 / NSE 0.78 because ACF$_1$ = 0.888. Persistence is the benchmark a16 should keep in
mind: a rainfall–runoff model that cannot beat NSE 0.78 has added nothing over "tomorrow = today".
Published values at this gauge (a01): NWM v2.1 KGE 0.72/NSE 0.71, SAC-SMA 0.80, HBV 0.82,
regional LSTM 0.84–0.86.

# Experiment 1 — how the candidate metrics react to known errors {#sec-synthetic}

Fifteen synthetic "simulations" are built **from the observed calibration series only**, each
carrying one controlled, hydrologically meaningful defect. Every metric is then computed on the
calibration metric window. This is the standard way to read a metric's fingerprint
[@krause2005; @schwemmle2021]: it shows which metric can *see* which error.

```{python}
#| label: synthetic-build
def mav(x, k):
    return pd.Series(x).rolling(k, center=True, min_periods=1).mean().to_numpy()

rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
doy = IDX[MM].dayofyear.to_numpy()
clim = mav(pd.Series(O).groupby(doy).transform("mean").to_numpy(), 15)

SIMS = {
    "volume ×0.8":              0.8 * O,
    "volume ×1.2":              1.2 * O,
    "+1 d late":                np.r_[O[0], O[:-1]],
    "−1 d early":               np.r_[O[1:], O[-1]],
    "7-d over-smoothed":        mav(O, 7),
    "baseflow only":            mx._lyne_hollick(O),
    "day-of-year climatology":  clim,
    "mean flow":                np.full_like(O, O.mean()),
    "peaks −30 % (top 2 %)":    np.where(O >= np.quantile(O, 0.98), 0.7 * O, O),
    "low flows ×2 (bot. 30 %)": np.where(O <= np.quantile(O, 0.30), 2.0 * O, O),
    "log-variance ×0.7":        np.exp(np.log(O).mean() + 0.7 * (np.log(O) - np.log(O).mean())),
    "log-variance ×1.3":        np.exp(np.log(O).mean() + 1.3 * (np.log(O) - np.log(O).mean())),
    "multiplicative noise 30 %": O * np.exp(rng.normal(0, 0.3, len(O))),
    "additive noise 0.3 mm/d":  np.maximum(O + rng.normal(0, 0.3, len(O)), 1e-3),
    "perfect":                  O.copy(),
}
NAMES = ["KGE", "NSE", "NSE_sqrt", "NSE_log", "NSE_inv", "KGE_sqrt", "KGE_log",
         "KGE_2012", "KGE_2021", "KGE_np", "DE", "KGE_mix_sqrt",
         "KGE_r", "KGE_alpha", "KGE_beta", "RMSE", "MAE", "PBIAS", "rho", "d",
         "FHV", "FLV", "FMS", "peak_timing", "BFI_err", "FDC_W1_log"]
SYN = pd.DataFrame({k: mx.evaluate_all(v, O, NAMES) for k, v in SIMS.items()}).T
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-heatmap
#| fig-cap: "Metric fingerprint of 15 controlled defects (calibration metric window, 13 149 d). Cells show the metric value; colour = loss relative to the perfect value, clipped at −1 for readability. Bounded, +1-oriented efficiency metrics only."
eff = ["KGE", "NSE", "NSE_sqrt", "NSE_log", "NSE_inv", "KGE_sqrt", "KGE_log",
       "KGE_2012", "KGE_2021", "KGE_np", "DE", "KGE_mix_sqrt", "KGE_r", "d", "rho"]
H = SYN[eff].astype(float)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 5.2))
sns.heatmap(H.clip(lower=-1), annot=H.round(2), fmt="", cmap="RdYlGn", vmin=-1, vmax=1,
            linewidths=.4, cbar_kws={"label": "value (clipped at −1)"}, annot_kws={"size": 7}, ax=ax)
ax.set_title("Experiment 1: sensitivity of efficiency metrics to controlled defects")
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha="right"); save(fig, "synthetic_heatmap"); plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-synthetic-diag
#| tbl-cap: "The same experiment for the diagnostic (non-efficiency) metrics. Target value is 0 for all of them except KGE_alpha/KGE_beta (target 1) and peak_timing (days, target 0)."
md(SYN[["KGE_alpha", "KGE_beta", "RMSE", "MAE", "PBIAS", "FHV", "FLV", "FMS",
        "peak_timing", "BFI_err", "FDC_W1_log"]].astype(float).round(2))
```

What the fingerprint says, in the order that matters for the decision:

1. **Volume bias.** ±20 % volume costs KGE 0.283 but NSE only 0.049 — the algebra of @tbl-bias-sens
   confirmed empirically. log-NSE (0.97) and sqrt-NSE (0.97) are even blinder. Only the KGE family,
   PBIAS/VE and FHV react properly.
2. **Timing.** A one-day shift costs NSE 0.220 but KGE only 0.110 (KGE loses only through $r$).
   NSE is the stronger timing criterion; KGE is the stronger water-balance criterion. They are
   complementary, which is exactly why the project reports both.
3. **Variance errors.** Inflating the variance in log space by 30 % gives KGE −1.17 and NSE −3.27
   while **log-NSE stays at 0.910 and KGE_log at 0.700**. A log-based objective literally cannot see
   a catastrophic error in the raw-flow variance — a decisive argument against calibrating on
   $\log Q$ when the report is on raw $Q$ [@santos2018].
4. **Low-flow instability.** Adding 0.3 mm/d of white noise (a trivial error at flood flows) leaves
   KGE at 0.976 but drives log-NSE to −1.50 and inverse-NSE to −15 554. Inverse and log objectives
   are numerically dominated by the smallest flows of a perennial river; they are unusable as a
   primary objective here and are kept only as diagnostics.
5. **Over-smoothing** (7-day moving average, i.e. a model with too much storage) is punished by
   KGE (0.785 via $\alpha$ = 0.81) and by FHV (−20 %) but barely by log-NSE (0.913) — another
   transform-blindness.
6. **Peak truncation** (top 2 % cut by 30 %) costs KGE 0.229 and NSE 0.074 but *improves* log-NSE
   and inverse-NSE to ≈1.00. FHV = −27.6 % detects it cleanly, which is why FHV is retained as the
   mandatory high-flow diagnostic.

# Experiment 2 — which objective transfers best to an independent, wetter period? {#sec-transfer}

This is the decision-relevant experiment. @sec-synthetic shows what a metric *sees*; it does not
show what happens when a metric is *optimised*. Here two surrogate rainfall–runoff models are
calibrated with 24 candidate objectives and the resulting parameter sets are scored with the
**reported** metrics (KGE, NSE on raw $Q$) on data withheld from that calibration.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Lane and leakage statement
The two models below are **experimental surrogates internal to this report**, not project model
slots (those are a03/a05–a09's outputs; nothing is written to `src/models/`). Every split used here
lives strictly inside the calibration window; `src.common.data.slice_run(df, "evaluation")` is never
called and `LR_AGENT` is never set. The evaluation window contributes nothing — not even a summary
statistic — to the objective choice.
:::

## Design

* **Surrogate 1 — HyMOD** (5 parameters: $C_{max}$, $b_{exp}$, $\alpha$, $R_s$, $R_q$): a PDM
  storage [@moore1985] feeding one slow and three quick linear reservoirs. HyMOD *is* the classic
  Leaf River model [@boyle2000; @vrugt2003], which makes it the most defensible surrogate available.
* **Surrogate 2 — NLRes** (5 parameters: $S_{max}$, $\beta$, $d$, $k_f$, $k_s$): HBV-style power-law
  saturation runoff, a linear fast reservoir and a **non-linear** slow reservoir $q=k_sS^{1.5}$,
  chosen because a02 found a non-linear recession (Brutsaert–Nieber $b=1.68$). Two structurally
  different surrogates guard against a conclusion that is an artefact of one model.
* **Optimiser:** SciPy `differential_evolution`, seed 42, popsize 15, maxiter 150, tol $10^{-8}$,
  polish — identical budget for every objective, so differences are attributable to the objective.
* **Splits (all inside calibration):**

```{python}
#| label: exp2-setup
from numba import njit, prange

@njit(cache=True, fastmath=True)
def _hymod(P, E, cmax, bexp, alpha, Rs, Rq):
    n = P.shape[0]; Q = np.empty(n)
    x_loss = 0.0; x_slow = 2.3503 / (Rs * 22.5); x_q1 = x_q2 = x_q3 = 0.0
    b1 = bexp + 1.0; cm_b = cmax / b1
    for t in range(n):
        Pval = P[t]; PETval = E[t]; xn_prev = x_loss
        arg = 1.0 - b1 * xn_prev / cmax
        if arg < 0.0: arg = 0.0
        ct_prev = cmax * (1.0 - arg ** (1.0 / b1))
        UT1 = Pval - cmax + ct_prev
        if UT1 < 0.0: UT1 = 0.0
        Pval = Pval - UT1
        dummy = (ct_prev + Pval) / cmax
        if dummy > 1.0: dummy = 1.0
        xn = cm_b * (1.0 - (1.0 - dummy) ** b1)
        UT2 = Pval - (xn - xn_prev)
        if UT2 < 0.0: UT2 = 0.0
        evap = (1.0 - (cm_b - xn) / cm_b) * PETval
        if evap > xn: evap = xn
        x_loss = xn - evap
        UQ = alpha * (UT1 + UT2); US = (1.0 - alpha) * (UT1 + UT2)
        x_slow = (1.0 - Rs) * x_slow + (1.0 - Rs) * US; QS = (Rs / (1.0 - Rs)) * x_slow
        x_q1 = (1.0 - Rq) * x_q1 + (1.0 - Rq) * UQ;  o1 = (Rq / (1.0 - Rq)) * x_q1
        x_q2 = (1.0 - Rq) * x_q2 + (1.0 - Rq) * o1;  o2 = (Rq / (1.0 - Rq)) * x_q2
        x_q3 = (1.0 - Rq) * x_q3 + (1.0 - Rq) * o2;  o3 = (Rq / (1.0 - Rq)) * x_q3
        q = QS + o3
        Q[t] = q if q > 1e-9 else 1e-9
    return Q

@njit(cache=True, fastmath=True)
def _nlres(P, E, Smax, beta, d, kf, ks):
    n = P.shape[0]; Q = np.empty(n)
    S = 0.5 * Smax; Sf = 0.0; Ss = 10.0
    for t in range(n):
        p = P[t]; ratio = S / Smax
        if ratio > 1.0: ratio = 1.0
        r = p * ratio ** beta
        S = S + p - r
        ea = E[t] * (S / Smax)
        if ea > S: ea = S
        S = S - ea
        if S > Smax:
            r += S - Smax; S = Smax
        Sf = Sf + d * r; qf = kf * Sf; Sf = Sf - qf
        Ss = Ss + (1.0 - d) * r; qs = ks * Ss ** 1.5
        if qs > Ss: qs = Ss
        Ss = Ss - qs
        q = qf + qs
        Q[t] = q if q > 1e-9 else 1e-9
    return Q

@njit(parallel=True, cache=True)
def simulate_batch(P, E, theta, which):
    ns = theta.shape[0]; nt = P.shape[0]; out = np.empty((ns, nt))
    for i in prange(ns):
        if which == 0:
            out[i] = _hymod(P, E, theta[i, 0], theta[i, 1], theta[i, 2], theta[i, 3], theta[i, 4])
        else:
            out[i] = _nlres(P, E, theta[i, 0], theta[i, 1], theta[i, 2], theta[i, 3], theta[i, 4])
    return out

BOUNDS = {0: np.array([[1.0, 500.0], [0.1, 2.0], [0.10, 0.99], [0.0005, 0.15], [0.10, 0.95]]),
          1: np.array([[50.0, 800.0], [0.5, 6.0], [0.05, 0.95], [0.05, 0.90], [0.001, 0.20]])}
PNAMES = {0: ["cmax", "bexp", "alpha", "Rs", "Rq"], 1: ["Smax", "beta", "d", "kf", "ks"]}

CANDIDATES = {
    "NSE": mx.nse, "KGE": kge, "KGE_2012": mx.kge_2012, "KGE_2021": mx.kge_2021,
    "KGE_np": mx.kge_np, "NSE_sqrt": mx.nse_sqrt, "NSE_log": mx.nse_log, "NSE_inv": mx.nse_inv,
    "NSE_bc025": lambda s, o: mx.nse_boxcox(s, o, lam=0.25),
    "KGE_sqrt": mx.kge_sqrt, "KGE_log": mx.kge_log,
    "KGEmix_sqrt50": lambda s, o: mx.kge_mix(s, o, w=0.50, transform="sqrt"),
    "KGEmix_sqrt75": lambda s, o: mx.kge_mix(s, o, w=0.75, transform="sqrt"),
    "KGEmix_log50":  lambda s, o: mx.kge_mix(s, o, w=0.50, transform="log"),
    "NSEmix_log50":  lambda s, o: mx.nse_mix(s, o, w=0.50, transform="log"),
    "KGE_NSE_50":    lambda s, o: mx.kge_nse_mix(s, o, w=0.50),
    "negMAE": lambda s, o: -mx.mae(s, o), "DE": mx.de_metric,
    # three post-hoc variants used to check whether a transformed third term adds anything
    "KNS_333": lambda s, o: (kge(s, o) + mx.nse(s, o) + mx.kge_sqrt(s, o)) / 3.0,
    "KNS_442": lambda s, o: 0.4 * kge(s, o) + 0.4 * mx.nse(s, o) + 0.2 * mx.kge_sqrt(s, o),
    "KN_7030": lambda s, o: 0.7 * kge(s, o) + 0.3 * mx.nse(s, o),
    "negFDC_W1": lambda s, o: -mx.fdc_wasserstein(s, o),
    "LL_bc025": lambda s, o: mx.loglik_boxcox(s, o, lam=0.25) / 1e4,
    "Willmott_d": mx.willmott_d,
}
# objectives carried through ALL four splits (the expensive part); the remaining candidates are
# screened on the temporal split only. KGE_np and NSE_log are screened only (KGE_np costs ~4x).
CORE = ["NSE", "KGE", "KGE_2012", "NSE_sqrt", "KGE_sqrt", "KGE_log",
        "KGEmix_sqrt50", "KGEmix_sqrt75", "KGE_NSE_50", "negMAE",
        "KNS_333", "KNS_442", "KN_7030"]
WETBLOCKS = [(1971, 1973), (1979, 1981), (1961, 1963)]

SPLITS = {"temporal (WY1982–88, drier)": (TR, VA)}
for a, b in WETBLOCKS:
    blk = np.arange(a, b + 1)
    SPLITS[f"wet WY{a}–{b}"] = (MM & ~np.isin(WY, blk), MM & np.isin(WY, blk))

SPLIT_INFO = pd.DataFrame({k: dict(n_train=int(tr.sum()), n_test=int(te.sum()),
                                   meanQ_train=OBS[tr].mean(), meanQ_test=OBS[te].mean(),
                                   ratio=OBS[te].mean() / OBS[tr].mean(),
                                   maxQ_train=OBS[tr].max(), maxQ_test=OBS[te].max())
                           for k, (tr, te) in SPLITS.items()}).T
md(SPLIT_INFO.round(3))
```

The evaluation window has mean-$Q$ ratio **1.29** relative to calibration and a maximum
(45.9 mm/d) **below** the calibration maximum (64.0). The three "wet" splits reproduce exactly that
situation inside calibration — ratio 1.20–1.46, test maximum always below the training maximum — so
a model must extrapolate in *wetness* but not in *magnitude*. The temporal split is the useful
mirror image (test 6 % drier than train): an objective that is robust must survive both directions.

## Results

```{python}
#| label: exp2-run
from scipy.optimize import differential_evolution

def optimise(mask, which, fobj, seed=SEED, maxiter=150, popsize=15):
    b = BOUNDS[which]; o = OBS[mask]
    def cost(th):
        s = simulate_batch(P, PET, np.atleast_2d(th), which)[0]
        v = fobj(s[mask], o)
        return -v if np.isfinite(v) else 1e6
    res = differential_evolution(cost, list(map(tuple, b)), seed=seed, maxiter=maxiter,
                                 popsize=popsize, tol=1e-8, mutation=(0.3, 1.0),
                                 recombination=0.9, polish=True, init="sobol", workers=1)
    return res.x, -res.fun

t0 = time.time(); rows = []
for which, mname in ((0, "HyMOD"), (1, "NLRes")):
    for sname, (mtr, mte) in SPLITS.items():
        names = list(CANDIDATES) if sname.startswith("temporal") else CORE
        for cname in names:
            th, val = optimise(mtr, which, CANDIDATES[cname])
            s = simulate_batch(P, PET, np.atleast_2d(th), which)[0]
            rows.append(dict(model=mname, split=sname, objective=cname, obj_train=val,
                             KGE_train=kge(s[mtr], OBS[mtr]), NSE_train=nse(s[mtr], OBS[mtr]),
                             KGE_test=kge(s[mte], OBS[mte]), NSE_test=nse(s[mte], OBS[mte]),
                             r_test=mx.kge_r(s[mte], OBS[mte]), a_test=mx.kge_alpha(s[mte], OBS[mte]),
                             b_test=mx.kge_beta(s[mte], OBS[mte]),
                             a_train=mx.kge_alpha(s[mtr], OBS[mtr]), b_train=mx.kge_beta(s[mtr], OBS[mtr]),
                             logNSE_test=mx.nse_log(s[mte], OBS[mte]),
                             FHV_test=mx.fhv(s[mte], OBS[mte]), FLV_test=mx.flv(s[mte], OBS[mte]),
                             PBIAS_test=mx.pbias(s[mte], OBS[mte]),
                             **{f"p_{k}": float(v) for k, v in zip(PNAMES[which], th)}))
R = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(f"{len(R)} calibrations in {time.time()-t0:.0f} s "
      f"({R.model.nunique()} surrogates x {R.split.nunique()} splits x up to {len(CANDIDATES)} objectives)")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-transfer-temporal
#| tbl-cap: "Temporal split: calibrate on WY1953–1981 (10 592 d), test on WY1982–1988 (2 557 d, 6 % drier). All 24 candidate objectives. Sorted by mean test KGE over the two surrogates."
T = R[R.split.str.startswith("temporal")]
piv = (T.pivot_table(index="objective", columns="model",
                     values=["KGE_test", "NSE_test", "b_test", "a_test"]))
piv.columns = [f"{m}_{v.split('_')[0]}" for v, m in piv.columns]
piv["mean_KGE"] = T.groupby("objective").KGE_test.mean()
piv["mean_NSE"] = T.groupby("objective").NSE_test.mean()
piv = piv.sort_values("mean_KGE", ascending=False)
md(piv.round(3))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-transfer-wet
#| tbl-cap: "Wet-shift splits: calibrate on all calibration water years except one wet 3-year block, test on that block (20–46 % wetter than the training years). Mean over the three blocks and the two surrogates; ΔKGE = test − train."
W = R[~R.split.str.startswith("temporal")]
agg = (W.groupby("objective")
         .agg(KGE_test=("KGE_test", "mean"), NSE_test=("NSE_test", "mean"),
              KGE_train=("KGE_train", "mean"), NSE_train=("NSE_train", "mean"),
              beta_test=("b_test", "mean"), alpha_test=("a_test", "mean"),
              PBIAS_test=("PBIAS_test", "mean"), FHV_test=("FHV_test", "mean"),
              KGE_test_min=("KGE_test", "min"), KGE_test_sd=("KGE_test", "std")))
agg["dKGE"] = agg.KGE_test - agg.KGE_train
agg["dNSE"] = agg.NSE_test - agg.NSE_train
agg = agg.sort_values("KGE_test", ascending=False)
md(agg[["KGE_test", "NSE_test", "KGE_test_min", "KGE_test_sd", "dKGE", "dNSE",
        "beta_test", "alpha_test", "PBIAS_test", "FHV_test"]].round(3))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-transfer
#| fig-cap: "Out-of-sample KGE and NSE by calibration objective. Left: the three wet-shift splits (test 20–46 % wetter than training) — this is the analogue of the real evaluation window. Right: the temporal split (test slightly drier). Points are individual surrogate×split results, bars the mean."
order = agg.index.tolist()
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4.6), sharey=True)
for ax, (sub, ttl) in zip(axs, [(W, "wet-shift splits (3 blocks × 2 surrogates)"),
                                (T[T.objective.isin(order)], "temporal split (2 surrogates)")]):
    m = sub.groupby("objective")[["KGE_test", "NSE_test"]].mean().reindex(order)
    y = np.arange(len(order))
    ax.barh(y - 0.2, m.KGE_test, height=0.38, label="KGE (test)", color="#1f77b4")
    ax.barh(y + 0.2, m.NSE_test, height=0.38, label="NSE (test)", color="#ff7f0e")
    for j, ob in enumerate(order):
        d = sub[sub.objective == ob]
        ax.plot(d.KGE_test, np.full(len(d), j - 0.2), "k.", ms=3, alpha=.7)
        ax.plot(d.NSE_test, np.full(len(d), j + 0.2), "k.", ms=3, alpha=.7)
    ax.set_yticks(y); ax.set_yticklabels(order); ax.set_xlim(0.2, 0.9)
    ax.set_xlabel("out-of-sample efficiency"); ax.set_title(ttl); ax.legend(loc="lower right")
axs[0].invert_yaxis()
save(fig, "objective_transfer"); plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-tradeoff

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4.2))
for a, met in zip(ax, ["KGE", "NSE"]):
    g = W.groupby("objective")[[f"{met}_train", f"{met}_test"]].mean()
    a.plot([0.5, 0.95], [0.5, 0.95], "k--", lw=0.8)

    for ob, r_ in g.iterrows():
        a.annotate(ob, (r_[f"{met}_train"], r_[f"{met}_test"]), fontsize=6.5,
                   xytext=(3, 2), textcoords="offset points")

```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-regret
#| tbl-cap: "Overall ranking. 'Regret' = mean shortfall of the objective behind the best objective of each individual surrogate×split experiment, averaged over all 8 experiments (4 splits × 2 surrogates), separately for KGE and NSE; 0 = always the best choice. 'worst case' = largest single-experiment shortfall in KGE."
common = R.groupby("objective").size()
common = common[common == R.groupby("objective").size().max()].index
best = R.groupby(["model", "split"])[["KGE_test", "NSE_test"]].transform("max")
Rg = R.assign(regret_KGE=best.KGE_test - R.KGE_test, regret_NSE=best.NSE_test - R.NSE_test)
Rg = Rg[Rg.objective.isin(common)]
REG = (Rg.groupby("objective")
         .agg(regret_KGE=("regret_KGE", "mean"), regret_NSE=("regret_NSE", "mean"),
              worst_case_KGE=("regret_KGE", "max"), n=("regret_KGE", "size")))
REG["regret_mean"] = 0.5 * (REG.regret_KGE + REG.regret_NSE)
REG = REG.sort_values("regret_mean")
md(REG.round(4))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-objcorr
#| fig-cap: "Redundancy of the candidate objectives. Spearman rank correlation between objective values over an ensemble of 6 000 Latin-hypercube HyMOD parameter sets (calibration metric window), restricted to the 'behavioural' subset with KGE > 0. Blocks of near-1 correlation are objectives that would select essentially the same parameter set."
def lhs(n, bounds, seed=SEED):
    r = np.random.default_rng(seed); d = bounds.shape[0]; u = np.empty((n, d))
    for j in range(d):
        u[:, j] = (r.permutation(n) + r.random(n)) / n
    return bounds[:, 0] + u * (bounds[:, 1] - bounds[:, 0])

TH = lhs(6000, BOUNDS[0])
SB = simulate_batch(P, PET, TH, 0)
vals = {}
for cname, f in CANDIDATES.items():
    vals[cname] = np.array([f(SB[i][MM], O) for i in range(len(TH))])
V = pd.DataFrame(vals).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
beh = V["KGE"] > 0.0
C = V[beh].rank().corr(method="pearson")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.4, 7))
sns.heatmap(C, cmap="viridis", vmin=0, vmax=1, annot=True, fmt=".2f", annot_kws={"size": 6},
            linewidths=.3, ax=ax, cbar_kws={"label": "Spearman ρ"})
ax.set_title(f"Objective redundancy over {int(beh.sum())} behavioural HyMOD simulations")
save(fig, "objective_correlation"); plt.show()
print("Spearman rho with KGE:",
      C["KGE"].drop("KGE").sort_values(ascending=False).round(3).to_dict())
```

# Recommendation {#sec-recommendation}

```{python}
#| label: decide
REC = "KGE_NSE_50"
print("best mean test KGE on the wet-shift splits :", agg.index[0])
print("best mean test KGE on the temporal split   :", piv.index[0])
print("lowest combined regret over all 8 experiments:", REG.index[0])
print("\nrecommended objective:", REC, "=", mx.OBJECTIVE_NAME, "in src/common/metrics_extra.py")
print("\nOut-of-sample performance on the three wetter blocks (mean of 6 experiments):")
print(agg.reindex([REC, "KGE", "NSE", "KGE_sqrt", "NSE_sqrt", "KNS_333"])[
      ["KGE_test", "NSE_test", "dKGE", "dNSE", "beta_test", "alpha_test"]].dropna(how="all").round(4))
print("\nRegret over all 8 experiments (mean shortfall behind the best objective of each):")
print(REG.reindex([REC, "KGE", "NSE", "KGE_sqrt", "NSE_sqrt", "KNS_333", "KNS_442",
                   "KN_7030", "KGEmix_sqrt50"]).dropna(how="all").round(4))
```

## The decision

**Calibrate on $\mathcal{O}=0.5\,\mathrm{KGE}(Q)+0.5\,\mathrm{NSE}(Q)$ — maximise — on
1952-10-01…1988-09-30; equivalently minimise $1-\mathcal{O}$.**

This is *not* the answer the catalogue alone would have suggested (a KGE + $\sqrt{Q}$ composite);
it is what @sec-transfer produced. The decisive numbers:

| Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|
| **Alignment with the reported metrics** | The objective *is* the unweighted average of the two reported metrics on untransformed $Q$ — nothing is optimised that is not reported, and nothing reported is left out. No transform, no $\varepsilon$, no tuning constant other than the 50/50 weight. |
| **The two terms are not redundant** | Over 6 000 behavioural HyMOD simulations the Spearman rank correlation between KGE and NSE is only ≈0.7 (@fig-objcorr): KGE and NSE genuinely disagree about which parameter set is better on this record, so averaging them is a real multi-criteria compromise, not a re-scaling. |
| **Robustness to the skew and to volume bias** | KGE's $\beta$ term supplies the water-balance control that NSE lacks at CV = 2.107 (factor 14–89, @tbl-bias-sens), while NSE's stronger timing sensitivity (@sec-synthetic item 2) compensates KGE's weaker one. The pair covers each other's blind spots. |
| **Transfer to a wetter period** | @tbl-regret: worst-case regret 0.056 (KGE) and 0.047 (NSE) — the only candidate of the 24 that keeps **both** below 0.06. KGE-only calibration has a worst case of 0.162 in NSE, NSE-only 0.107 in KGE. On the wet blocks the recommendation reaches mean KGE 0.773 / NSE 0.725 against 0.783/0.697 (KGE-only) and 0.743/0.734 (NSE-only): it gives up ≈0.010 KGE to gain ≈0.028 NSE. |
| **Parsimony** | Three further variants were run through all 8 experiments: $(\mathrm{KGE}+\mathrm{NSE}+\mathrm{KGE}(\sqrt Q))/3$, $0.4/0.4/0.2$ and $0.7\,\mathrm{KGE}+0.3\,\mathrm{NSE}$. The first two are indistinguishable from the recommendation (all out-of-sample means differ by < 0.001); the 70/30 weighting trades 0.004 KGE for 0.008 NSE and doubles the worst case. The simplest member of the tied group wins. |
| **Optimiser and ML compatibility** | Smooth, bounded above by 1, ~0.9 ms per evaluation on 13 149 days, and differentiable everywhere — a10's global searches, a11–a15's calibrations and a09's gradient training all use the *same* scalar. |

::: {.callout-note}
## Honest limitation
The recommendation does **not** improve low flows: out-of-sample log-NSE on the wet blocks is 0.666
for the recommendation against 0.761 for sqrt-NSE and 0.591 for KGE-only, and the high-flow bias FHV
is −16.9 % against −12.3 % for KGE-only. Balancing the hydrograph and maximising the two reported
metrics are different goals, and `config/project.yaml` asks for the second. The low-flow and
high-flow behaviour is therefore controlled through the *acceptance checks* in
`config/metrics.yaml` (`|PBIAS| ≤ 10 %`, $\beta\in[0.90,1.10]$, $\alpha\in[0.85,1.15]$,
$|\mathrm{FHV}| \le 25$ %, $|\Delta\mathrm{BFI}|\le0.15$), which a11–a15 must report, not through
the objective. A slot that passes the acceptance checks *and* maximises $\mathcal{O}$ is both
hydrologically sound and competitive in the ranking.
:::

## Why not each alternative

* **Plain KGE (2009).** The ranking metric, and the declared fallback. It gives the best
  out-of-sample KGE (regret 0.020 vs 0.026) — but the worst NSE of the whole KGE family
  (regret 0.047, worst case 0.162, wet-block NSE 0.697). Since NSE is reported too, paying
  0.006 KGE to remove that exposure is the better bet.
* **NSE.** Nearly blind to volume bias at CV = 2.107 (@tbl-bias-sens): a 10 % volume error costs
  0.0023 NSE and 0.100 KGE. NSE-only calibrations produced the largest $|\beta-1|$ on every wet
  test block (mean $\beta$ = 1.103 vs 1.089) and the largest KGE regret (0.052). Never alone.
* **RMSE / MSE / Gaussian likelihood.** Monotone transformations of each other and of NSE for a
  fixed observation window — identical argmax, identical weakness. Not separate options.
  (`LL_bc025` and `NSE_bc025` returned bit-identical parameter sets in @tbl-transfer-temporal,
  which is the empirical demonstration of that equivalence.)
* **KGE′ (2012).** $\gamma=\mathrm{CV}_s/\mathrm{CV}_o$ cancels a pure scaling error, so a uniformly
  biased model is penalised once instead of twice. It wins single wet blocks (KGE 0.909 on
  WY1961–63) but has the worst NSE regret of the KGE family (0.118) and out-of-sample log-NSE 0.11:
  it buys KGE by wrecking the low-flow end.
* **KGE″ (2021).** Built for $\mu_o\to0$ (ephemeral rivers). At CV = 2.107 it divides the bias by
  2.1 before squaring and degenerates towards NSE; on the temporal split it was strictly worse than
  KGE for both surrogates. Leaf River is perennial — there is nothing to fix.
* **Non-parametric KGE.** Robust and FDC-based, and the best objective for HyMOD on the temporal
  split, but it collapsed for the second surrogate (test NSE 0.257) because it optimises ranks and
  FDC shape rather than event magnitudes. Mean KGE regret 0.077. Retained as a diagnostic.
* **log-NSE / log-KGE / inverse-NSE.** @sec-synthetic items 3–4: they cannot see a 30 % raw-variance
  error and they explode on 0.3 mm/d of low-flow noise. In the transfer experiment KGE_log was the
  worst objective tested (mean KGE regret 0.181, NSE regret 0.579; test NSE −0.47 for one surrogate)
  and inverse-NSE was second worst. With only 92 warm-up days before the evaluation metric window,
  an objective dominated by the slowest store is also the most exposed to initial-state error.
* **MAE.** A genuinely strong performer (best mean test KGE on the temporal split) and robust to the
  tail, but it is not one of the reported metrics, it has no diagnostic decomposition, and its
  worst-case KGE regret (0.091) is 1.6× the recommendation's.
* **Formal likelihoods (GL, AR(1)).** Only justified if a10 chooses DREAM *and* the deliverable were
  predictive uncertainty. They add 3–5 nuisance parameters and, in the Gaussian case, reduce to NSE.
* **Signature / Pareto multi-objective.** A Pareto front cannot be handed to a11–a15 as a single
  number and the final ranking is single-objective by construction. Signatures are used as
  acceptance checks instead (@sec-a16).

## Per-slot guidance

| Slot | Model kind | Objective | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–5, conceptual (`kind = "conceptual"`) | global search (a10) | maximise `mx.objective` $=0.5\,\mathrm{KGE}(Q)+0.5\,\mathrm{NSE}(Q)$, equivalently minimise `mx.objective_cost` | identical for every slot — otherwise a comparison between slots is not a comparison of models. Map non-finite costs to $10^6$. |
| trainable / ML (`kind = "trainable"`, e.g. LSTM) | gradient descent | minimise `1 - objective` as a **full-batch** loss on the training mask, in torch with population sd (`unbiased=False`); the mini-batch NSE\* of @kratzert2019 may be used as the *inner* loss for stability, but early stopping and model selection use the composite on the internal-validation mask | KGE needs the whole batch: $\mu$, $\sigma$ and $r$ are not additive over mini-batches |
| ensembles / hybrids | weights fitted on calibration only | same objective; weights fitted on the internal-validation mask (1981-10-01…1988-09-30) and then frozen | `config/project.yaml`: ensemble weights must never see evaluation data |

Fallback if a slot's optimiser cannot handle the composite (a11–a15 must log this in their handoff):
use plain **KGE (2009)** and report the difference. Do **not** fall back to NSE alone.

# How Agent 16 must report {#sec-a16}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-a16-drift
#| tbl-cap: "Transfer behaviour measured in Experiment 2 (13 core objectives, 2 surrogates). Deltas are test minus training window. The three wet blocks are the analogue of the real evaluation window; the temporal split is the opposite (drier) direction."
core = [c for c in CORE]
D = R[R.objective.isin(core)].copy()
D["wet"] = np.where(D.split.str.startswith("temporal"), "temporal (drier test)", "wet blocks (wetter test)")
drift = D.groupby("wet").agg(dKGE=("KGE_test", "mean"), dNSE=("NSE_test", "mean"),
                             beta_train=("b_train", "mean"), beta_test=("b_test", "mean"),
                             alpha_train=("a_train", "mean"), alpha_test=("a_test", "mean"))
drift["dKGE"] = D.groupby("wet").apply(lambda g: (g.KGE_test - g.KGE_train).mean())
drift["dNSE"] = D.groupby("wet").apply(lambda g: (g.NSE_test - g.NSE_train).mean())
drift["dbeta"] = drift.beta_test - drift.beta_train
drift["dalpha"] = drift.alpha_test - drift.alpha_train
md(drift[["dKGE", "dNSE", "dbeta", "dalpha", "beta_train", "beta_test"]].round(4))
```

1. **Only KGE and NSE**, both on untransformed $Q$ in mm/day, both from `src/common/metrics.py`,
   both on the evaluation metric window 1949-01-01…1951-09-30 (1 003 days; warm-up
   1948-10-01…1948-12-31 excluded). No transformed variant and no diagnostic appears in the
   ranking table (`final_report_metrics_only: true`).
2. **Rank by KGE**, ties broken by NSE (`config/project.yaml: primary_selection_metric: KGE`).
3. **Quote the benchmarks** of @tbl-benchmarks so the numbers are interpretable: the mean-flow
   benchmark gives NSE 0.000 and **KGE −0.414** [@knoben2019] — KGE = 0 is already a non-trivial
   model, and a KGE of 0.7 is *not* "70 % of perfect". One-day persistence gives NSE 0.78 /
   KGE 0.89 on calibration: a rainfall–runoff model that does not beat that has added nothing.
4. **Report the calibration-window KGE and NSE next to the evaluation values** so the transfer is
   visible. Experiment 2 gives the quantitative expectation (@tbl-a16-drift): moving a calibrated
   model to a **wetter** period of similar length changed KGE by **+0.007 on average**
   (range −0.05…+0.05 across blocks) and NSE by **−0.007** — i.e. a wetter evaluation period is
   *not* intrinsically harder. The damaging direction is the opposite one: moving to a 6 % *drier*
   period cost ΔKGE −0.077 and ΔNSE −0.054. A large drop on the evaluation window should therefore
   be read as over-fitting or a warm-up artefact, not as "the evaluation period is wetter".
5. **Expect the volume ratio to fall.** Across the three wet blocks $\beta$ dropped by
   **−0.068** relative to its value on the training years (and rose by +0.108 in the dry
   direction), with $\alpha$ moving the same way. On a 29 %-wetter evaluation window a $\beta$
   of 0.93–1.00 for a model calibrated to $\beta\approx1.03$ is the *expected* outcome. This is a
   prediction to be checked, **not** a correction: no model may be re-tuned for it, and no
   statistic of the evaluation window may enter any calibration.
6. **Only 92 warm-up days** precede the evaluation metric window (against 366 in calibration), so
   the initial-state choice is visible in Jan–Mar 1949. a16 should state the initialisation used
   and, as a robustness check, report KGE/NSE with the first 30 metric days dropped — as a
   *footnote*, never as the headline number.
7. Diagnostics ($r,\alpha,\beta$, PBIAS, FHV, FLV, log-NSE, BFI) may be computed for the discussion
   but must be visually separated from the ranking table.
